items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Perry Como. It was good, professionally-made stuff... Perry Como has got a very good voice and everything like that

ctx.x: Was it partly the fact that jazz came from America? Or was it just the music itself?

No, it was like, they thought of jazz, oh well, that’s kind of the music of, it was the young people, it was something that they didn’t understand, it had nothing to do with America. They didn’t know where it came from probably. And yet my mother always liked the popular songs of the day, but popular music then was a pretty, sort of a bland affair. You had people like I remember like Guy Mitchell and Jo Stafford, and these sort of people. There wasn’t anything gutsy or anything to offend the ears. Perry Como. It…
Did the American songwriters of the 30s and 40s, did their songs make it over to England?
